items.summary: AutoGPT Platform versions 0.6.26 through 0.7.4 ship a publicly known, hardcoded default JWT verification key, so anyone who knows the secret can forge valid tokens for any user or for the admin role and bypass authentication without user interaction. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.0.
items.plain: AutoGPT lets anyone forge a login for any account, including admins — upgrade to version 0.8.0 now.

items.summary: Improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network. Microsoft lists SharePoint Server Subscription Edition builds from 16.0.0 before 16.0.20326.20190 as affected, alongside SharePoint Online.
items.plain: Microsoft SharePoint lets a logged-in attacker run code on the server — apply the Microsoft security update now.
items.product: Microsoft SharePoint Online / Microsoft SharePoint Server Subscription Edition

items.summary: A vulnerability in the database service of Cisco Expressway Series, due to persistent cookies and insufficient validation of client certificates when TLS Verify Mode is enabled for clustering, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on November 20 after reported exploitation; Cisco fixes it in X15.5.20.
items.plain: Cisco Expressway lets attackers run commands as the top administrator without logging in and is being exploited — upgrade now.

items.summary: Code injection in Cribl Stream's REST Collector pagination: an attacker who controls pagination data returned by an upstream API or service queried by an existing REST Collector can execute code with the Worker service account's permissions during a job run. Cribl's solution is to upgrade Cribl Stream to v4.21.
items.plain: Cribl Stream can be tricked by a connected data source into running an attacker's code — upgrade to version 4.21 now.

items.summary: rConfig Core 8.0.0 before 8.2.17 and rConfig Pro before 8.4.0 contain a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Config Search View Matches dialog, which renders configuration context via v-html without escaping. Attackers can place markup in device banners, descriptions or locations to execute script in a user's session and read stored configurations containing secrets.
items.plain: rConfig can let an attacker run script in a user's session and read stored network configurations — upgrade to a fixed release now.
